newsitem.title: USA: INTERVIEW-Rio Hotel & Casino traffic strong.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW-Rio Hotel & Casino traffic strong.

text.p: Rio Hotel & Casino Inc President Jay Barrett on Friday said the new Masquerade Village in the Rio Hotel in Las Vegas has opened to strong traffic, but he does not expect the project to begin boosting earnings until the second half of the year.

In an interview, Barrett agreed with financial analysts that operating earnings for the first quarter ending March 31 were likely to be near the low end of a range of estimates between $0.18 to $0.29 a share, before pre-opening costs.
He also said it was too soon to know exactly how high the pre-opening costs would run.
Rio is near completion of its $200 million master plan, including Masquerade Village. The program will boost total room count to more than 2,500 rooms and add retail shops and casino space.
To fill the new rooms and casino, the all-suite hotel must rely on tourist traffic, which concerns investors because Rio's core revenues historically have come from local residents.
Barrett said the customer mix should shift to between 70 and 80 percent tourists by 1998. Currently 70 percent of its customers are locals and 30 percent tourists.
Still, the initial response to Masquerade Village shows local residents are sticking around.
"The preliminary results are very, very good," he said. "The new rooms we've added have been occupied and the rates consistent with the past, maybe a little higher."
